editorial:
You follow Mark Zuckerberg as he turns a dorm-room idea into Facebook, while friendships and trust fall apart around him. The story moves between coding sessions, campus life, and tense legal meetings, so you always feel the pressure building. Jesse Eisenberg plays Mark as sharp, awkward, and hard to read, while Andrew Garfield brings real heart as Eduardo. The movie feels smart but never boring, with quick dialogue, a cold driven mood, and a strong sense that every choice has a cost.

The acting is excellent, the pacing stays fast, and the soundtrack gives every scene extra energy. You get a clear look at ambition, betrayal, and success, though some viewers may want more warmth from the main character. If you like true stories about power and money, this is a great pick for a weekend watch. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the end, Mark settles the lawsuits and keeps control of Facebook, but he loses Eduardo as a friend. The final twist is that all his money and power still leave him alone, refreshing an old girlfriend's profile page while waiting for a friend request. It shows that winning the business battle did not fix the personal damage. You see him sitting alone at his laptop, still chasing connection.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about ambition, tech, and complicated friendships.
